title: Stage 01 — Mathematics
description: Linear algebra, calculus, and analysis for models.

questions.prompt: What does the dot product of two centered vectors measure (up to a scale)?
choices: The determinant of the data matrix
questions.explanation: After centering, a·b = Σ (x−x̄)(y−ȳ), which is (n−1) times sample covariance.

questions.prompt: Linear regression prediction ŷ = w·x is best described as:
questions.explanation: Each feature is multiplied by a weight and summed — a dot product.

questions.prompt: PCA keeps eigenvectors of which matrix (centered data)?
questions.explanation: Principal axes are eigenvectors of the covariance (or singular vectors of the data matrix).

questions.prompt: If two columns of X are identical, XᵀX is typically:
questions.explanation: Perfect collinearity makes the Gram matrix singular; OLS has no unique solution.
V aligns input directions, Σ stretches, U maps to the output basis.

questions.prompt: In w ← w − η∇L, η is:
questions.explanation: η scales the step. Too large overshoots; too small crawls.

choices: The chain rule on a computation graph
questions.explanation: Local derivatives multiply along paths from weights to the loss.

choices: A product of many small derivatives collapses to ~0
questions.explanation: Sigmoid/tanh saturation and long unrolled nets make the product tiny.

questions.prompt: A convex smooth loss means local minima are:
questions.explanation: Convexity: any local min is global. Deep nets are generally not convex.

questions.prompt: L2 regularization is the Lagrangian cousin of:
questions.explanation: Ridge corresponds to a Euclidean ball constraint on weights.

questions.prompt: Why train with cross-entropy rather than accuracy?
choices: Accuracy is discontinuous / flat almost everywhere, so gradients vanish
questions.explanation: Accuracy does not give useful gradients for SGD.

questions.prompt: The Hessian of a loss is:
choices: First derivatives of a vector map
Second derivatives of a scalar loss
questions.explanation: Hᵢⱼ = ∂²L/∂wᵢ∂wⱼ. PSD Hessian relates to convexity.

questions.prompt: Cosine similarity is a dot product after:
questions.explanation: On the unit sphere, a·b = cos θ.

questions.prompt: Attention scores before softmax are typically:
choices: Convolutions of Q with a 3×3 kernel
Scaled dot products between queries and keys

questions.prompt: Exploding gradients mean the composition is locally:
questions.explanation: Clipping is a blunt cap on that steepness.

questions.prompt: For a single point x=2, y=5 and ŷ=w₁x+w₀, many (w₀,w₁) fit. This is:
questions.explanation: Two parameters, one observation: a line of solutions.
